entries.claim: Treat the post-smoke phase-diagram boundary as coming from tuned overlap credits / thresholds on synthetic FO/CN data.
entries.reason: GENERAL throughput-formula bug, not tuning. On a correct speculative hit the wall accumulator still added duration_ns (serial charge), so overlap credit was structurally absent for every policy and every dataset. Comment claimed overlap hid the cost; code did not. Fix: hit_path_wall_ns(credit_overlap=True) omits duration_ns on hits; pays only extra-sibling waste.
evidence: Before (bug): wall += dur on hit (plus extras waste) — equivalent to hit_path_wall_ns(..., credit_overlap=False)
After (fix): wall += penalty_ns * extras only on hit — hit_path_wall_ns(..., credit_overlap=True)
tests/tlp01/test_overlap_credit.py — fails under pre-fix formula, passes under post-fix

entries.claim: M1–M5 speedup vs recorded wall-clock makespan measures turn-level parallelism.
entries.reason: On live S2 traces, recorded wall includes LLM/harness idle between events that is absent from per-event duration_ns. Fully serial Tier-C DAGs (max_in_flight=1) still showed ~3× 'speedup' by removing idle. Correct denominator for the limit study is simulate_in_order_work (serial schedule of the same unit costs). G-V continues to use recorded wall via simulate_in_order.

entries.claim: T2 ceiling taxonomy (track 2a) and frontier boundary (track 1b) are quotable as reported in t2_ladder_report.md.
entries.reason: Check A FAIL: MT-SER-02 Tier-S M1 max speedup 1.72× > 1.5× bound after work-baseline fix. Tier-C is clean (1.0×); SER-01 both tiers ≤1.01×. SER-02 traces are retry fan-outs (many code_exec ← retrieve) not the pre-registered 3-step serial chain — control contamination plus Tier-S allowing sibling width. Pre-registered disposition: both tracks SUSPENDED; nothing quotable until controls pass or are re-collected as true serial chains.

entries.claim: Check A SER-02 Tier-S 1.72x is caused by Tier-S missing dep_refs and/or allowing code_exec sibling width under retry fan-out.
entries.reason: False mechanism. On all five SER-02 seeds Tier-0 ⊆ Tier-S already holds (dep_refs recovered via result_id_ref / from_result= in input_text). Retry siblings are fully connected under Tier-S (136/136 sibling pairs on s3). The 1.40–1.72x is entirely turn∥tools overlap under M1 break_control=True: Tier-S has no data edge 0→1 while Tier-C adds positional_adjacency 0→1. Counterfactual adding data edge 0→first_tool collapses every SER-02 Tier-S M1 speedup to 1.000. SER-01 passes because tool_work is ~1% of turn_work so hiding the turn barely moves the ratio.

entries.claim: Tier-0 ⊆ Tier-S need not be gated because Tier-0 ⊆ Tier-C suffices.
entries.reason: Omission. dep_refs are Tier-S-class evidence by construction. Protocol/gate previously required only Tier-0 ⊆ Tier-C. Fixed: tier_s_edges unions Tier-0; assert_tier0_subseteq_tier_s in G-D; protocol_tlp01_v2.json tier0_subseteq_tier_s. On the frozen S2 corpus this is edge-set inert (already ⊆ via string match) — not the Check A root cause — but closes the hole permanently.

entries.claim: Check A 'M1 speedup ≤1.2 / fail >1.5 on either tier' is a calibrated negative-control test of tool-chain seriality under current M1 semantics.
entries.reason: Miscalibrated. M1 sets break_control=True, so planning-turn cost may hide under a data-serial tool chain. Any session with substantial tool_work relative to turn_work then reports M1 speedup ≈ work/tool_work even with a perfect serial tool DAG. SER-02 (turn/work 0.28–0.42) trips >1.5; SER-01 (turn/work ≈0.99) does not. Control lesson: either evaluate tool-only makespans for Check A, or require an explicit turn→first_tool data edge in the control metric — do not treat raw M1 Tier-S>1.5 on SER-02 as proof of oracle-invented tool parallelism. Rungs remain SUSPENDED until Check A is redefined and A–G re-run.
evidence: extract.py comment: M1 breaks control edges

entries.claim: Dependence graphs need only data/control kinds; Check A miscalibration (#10) is the root SER-02 issue.
entries.reason: Category error. The graph layer had no edge taxonomy. SC-EMIT (turn→tools it emits) is an ordering fact that is neither data dependence nor content-discoverable. Legacy M1 broke unclassified control edges via break_control=True, so Check A's ≈1x expectation was written for M1a semantics but applied to M1b. Taxonomy v2 classifies SC-EMIT/SD-*/HO/D*; machines declare breakable classes. SER-02's 1.72x is M1b speculation headroom, not a bug.

entries.claim: Unqualified M1 is a valid machine-model label.
entries.reason: Retired. Split into M1a (breaks HO only — width ceiling, no speculation) and M1b (breaks HO+SC — perfect control speculation). Ceiling rungs evaluate M1a; speculation headroom is M1b/M1a reported unverdicted.
